done_when: A failed forge-pr-check prints its refusal reasons and next step in the GitHub job log.

known.title: Not done: A failed forge-pr-check prints its refusal reasons and next step in the GitHub job log.
Test: A failed forge-pr-check prints its refusal reasons and next step in the GitHub job log.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done - A proof list that names a missing test produces a refusal without a next step.
Case: normal use - A builder renames a test or records its name incorrectly in the Proof list. `src/forge/proof.py:214` emits only that the test is not on the branch; `src/forge/prcheck.py:548` prints that message and returns failure. Capturing both streams puts the reason in the report, but there is still no guidance to correct the name or commit the test.
findings.title: Not done: A failed forge-pr-check prints its refusal reasons and next step in the GitHub job log.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test - The named proof exercises only a missing Proof list entry and misses the existing refusal for a named test that is absent from the branch.
Case: normal use - A Proof list contains an incorrect or outdated test name. The assertions at the end of this test still pass for their separate no-entry scenario even though `src/forge/proof.py:214` supplies no next step for the absent-test refusal.
findings.title: Test: A failed forge-pr-check prints its refusal reasons and next step in the GitHub job log.

why: When forge-pr-check fails on GitHub, the job log printed by the Report review status step is empty, so the real reason is hidden and close suggests a new build round (issue #1803).
